summary: Parents whose child won a seat in free all-day pre-K worked more hours and earned more for years afterward.
realLife: New Haven gave seats in free full-day public pre-K for 3 and 4 year olds by lottery, so researchers compared winning and non-winning families. Parents of winners earned about $5,461 more a year, up 21.7 percent, while the child was pre-K age, and worked about 12.8 more hours a week the next year. The gain in earnings lasted at least six more years even as the hours effect faded. The page found no statistically significant effect on the children's test scores.
sources: https://www.nber.org/digest/202502/universal-pre-k-access-and-parental-earnings (NBER Digest on universal pre-K and parents' earnings)
